spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Chapter


---


**¶2.
** The evil
 that issued from the ruling falsities —
 which is the very
 substance of spiritual
 corruption — rose up toward the visible form
 of Divine Truth as
 it was
 made
 manifest
.
 It was sev
ered from that sphere
 and descended into the external natural mind,
 for it could not be received within the
 rational faculty. When it entered
 the external natural mind it
 formed a perverted perception.
 It ro
oted itself within
 that disordered perception and produced corresponding
 evil works. And
 when the m
onstrous and
 incomplete affections fell
 down
 into the natural mind a second time…


**¶3.** …
within
 those
 evil works, the corruption
 assumed them and became articulate in the
 dominant
 falsity that governed the
 rest
. That
 ruling
 falsity says
 to its companions
: *
Surrender your wisdom to me, and I
 will fashion for you a form of understanding
 modeled upon
 the likeness of the Divine.*
 What it commanded
, they performed
:
 they surrendered their remaining wisdom, and
 the dominant falsity fashioned an
 imitation form
.


**¶4.** The
 evil that issued from the ruling falsities
 — which is the spiritual corruption that perceived
 the visible form of Divine Truth and that
 formed a perverted perception and rooted
 itself within it — afterward it rose up
 through
 the evil works. It passed
 into
 the ruling falsities…
 they fashioned the will and the
 understanding of the earliest humanity
 after the likeness of the Divine.
 Through the energy of the evil that had
 perceived the visible form of Divine Truth,
 it entered
 the ruling falsities by
 way
 of those
 evil works. It assumed them,
 and they too sculpted… they generated
 each faculty according to its appointed
 tendency
;
 some faculties bore
 resemb
lance to the Divine, others did
 not.

**¶5.
** This teaches how the ruling falsities
 shaped the will and understanding of the earliest
 humanity through
 the activity
 of the evil that entered them by
 way
 of perverted works, and how that
 human
 form
 was ordained after the image
 of the Divine.

**¶
6.** The shaping power arranged
 within the form of the will and the
 understanding both
 external and internal faculties, for both
 perception and activity. Each faculty was ap
portioned its own domain in
 the
 mind
. For everything that the perceptions and
 constituent elements receive from without, there exist
 internal memory-stores, repositories, and
 receptive capacities; and what is
 received into them is preserved within them.
 Whenever they are called
 upon to deliver what has
 been depos
ited in their inner
 memory, they bring forth
 what they have received and deliver it to
 the inquiring faculty that sought it.


**¶7.** In
 this way each faculty… its
 external capacities,
 to perceive… every type within…


**¶8.** Also
, the faculty of intellectual sight poss
esses its own domains and
 receptive capacities and
 repositories and
 memory-stores within, so that every
 form of understanding it might perceive —
 whether good or evil, whether lovely or
 detestable or lustful — it
 can receive into its memory. Also,
 when the faculty of intellectual sight is moved
 to send forth the representation
 it perceived and took in, it can
 enter its memory-stores at any time
 and
 reflect upon
 and seek… and it brings the
 form
 forth
 and delivers it to the inquiring faculty
 that requested it and the one that desired
 it — whether it be something from conc
upiscence… or a representation
 of love… or something hateful.
 And thus shall the
 faculty of understanding produce and accomplish what it
 does in each kind
.

**¶9.**
 The faculty of obedience and
 recept
ivity
 to
 truth poss
esses its own memory-stores also
. Every influx it
 might
 receive — whether good or evil — shall
 be taken in and placed in its domains
 and inner
 repositories, and it is guarded there
 for an
 entire period. After the
 full period, if any faculty comes and
 inqu
ires of
 it
 concerning
 the truth or
 fals
ity that was heard at a given time
 and taken
 into its memory, immediately it shall enter
 its repositories and seek and review and search
 after this word, and send it forth
 from where it was first placed, the
 domain in which it was kept.


**¶10.** In like
 order
, the faculty of interior perception — the
 disc
ernment of spiritual
 quality
 — shall function just as that
 of the
 understanding and that of obedience.
 Every interior quality it discerns it
 shall take into
 itself and deposit in its inner memory.
 Whenever it is questioned
 by an inquiring faculty, it shall
 enter its memory-store and recall…
 only
 these things.

**¶11
.** However, even the faculty of
 expression and confession,
 and the faculty of discerning good
, have a power dwelling in them.
 That faculty of discerning good poss
esses receptive capacities and repositories set
 apart for it. It too receives these
 perceptions of spiritual
 quality and gathers them in. And
 at any moment when inquiry is made concerning
 a quality of good or
 evil, it shall send it forth and
 recall that quality. It shall capture and
 deliver even the distingu
ishing character of that good; it
 shall give its memory to the inquiring
 faculty that asks
 for it.

**¶12
.** Again
, the faculty of outward contact and
 communication
 with
 external things is
 also
 so: when it touches
,
 that
 contact shall im
press
 its memory. And it takes it into
 its inner repository until some faculty asks for
 the memory. Immediately it shall enter
 again and bring forth
 the memory of this contact that
 was
 made, and give it to whatever asks
 for it.

**¶13
.** And the faculty of the will
 — which
 rules
 over them all — is the
 most fully
 constit
uted in
 this
 manner
. Everything
 that the five faculties receive and place
 in store for the will, the will
 shall receive and guard. Any time they
 request
 what they depos
ited,
 it shall send out and return
 everything they gave to it.

**
¶14.** For the counsel
 of the will is like the ruling love
 of
 the whole
 person
. All the subordinate affections of
 its domain and all
 the leading principles of its activity are placed
 under
 it. Any time these
 leading principles petition
 it for whatever they require, it shall
 give them the guidance and direction by which
 they act.

**¶15
.** Furthermore, the
 will
 is like a containing form: everything that
 is entrusted to it by the
 faculties, and given over
,
 it shall receive and place in separate containing
 forms and domains. Any time…


**¶16.** …in
 the domain where it placed it.


**¶17.** This is
 also the way of the faculty that
 gov
erns the external person. The understanding that
 intellectual sight perceives and delivers to it
 —
 upon
 receiving
 it, the
 faculty
 shall bring it forth again from the memory
 wherein it had placed it,
 and give it to whatever asks for it
.

**¶18.**
 Again, the truth
 that obedience receives
 and delivers to it — upon receiving it
 from
 that
 faculty —
 at
 any time when inquiry is made for that
 truth, it shall bring forth and give
 the perception of obedience to whatever
 has asked.
 It
 shall bring
 forth and deliver the infl
ux of ob
edience to whatever has inqu
ired.


**¶19.** Again
, the faculty of interior perception follows this
 same pattern; and that of discer
ning good is of the same type.
 Outward contact… they shall bring
 it forth… And whenever inquiry
 is made,
 it shall bring it forth and deliver it
.

**¶20.**
 Indeed, protective principles stand at the open
ings of the mind guarding them,
 and restraints are fastened upon those
 openings under the control of the protective
 principles that guard them.

**
¶21.** Just as protective principles
 guard an
 ordered
 mind with elevated stations and posts of vigil
ance —
 as the containing domains open
 out
 from there and the restraints are upon
 the points of entry — the
 guardians control the restraints while
 they stand watch at the thresholds
 of
 vigil
ance. So whatever
 belongs to the mind's own ruling love
 as concordant with its
 quality
, belonging to its own sphere
 — for this the guardians shall
 open the entry and receive it will
ingly.
 However, what is foreign and contrary to
 the ruling love they prevent, and leave
 standing
 at the threshold. They shall not yield
 to let it enter. Again, another
 influence which they do receive, they admit
 with great reluct
ance,
 and
 there are many containing domains… the number
 of restraints… Whenever someone w
ills
… the restraint
 at hand, opens the entry and brings
 forth whatever is hidden within.

**
¶22.** This external person
 is like the great
 ordered mind. And the openings of
 that
 mind with their guardians are like the
 faculties and organs of the external person
. Now, the openings of the
 external person are understanding, obedience
, and interior perception; and the fac
ulties that send forth
 expression. There are many sentinels
 and a multitude of guardians placed
 over the capacities of the external person
, guarding its openings. And
 the faculty within is
 the directing principle of the external person,
 the sovereign of the entire ordered mind;
 so that whenever it w
ills it can open, and
 whenever
 it wills it can close.


**¶23.** However,
 when
 the Divine Truth operating
 within — the Light of
 the interior
 mind — comes, it shall turn toward
 the openings of the external person.
 The ruling falsities, which
 are the guardians at
 the thresholds, shall hinder
 and restrain it from entering. They
 shall bind the circuit of the external person
 so that this power,
 foreign to their dominion, cannot enter
 it.

**¶24.
** Nevertheless, the Divine Truth within,
 by its wisdom and its
 reverence and its perseverance,
 shall humble the ruling falsities set
 at the openings of the external person
. When it finishes humbling them
 it
 shall take from them the restraints upon
 all
 the openings. Now, those
 openings that had been opened before to
 the displays of concupiscence —
 to receive the perceptions of sensual
 pleasure, to convey the persuas
ions of worldly concern, to receive
 the grat
ifications of various indulgences and imp
ure satisfactions together with the evil within
 them — whoever ceases to receive these
, his will and understanding shall follow after
 the Divine.

**¶25
.** So now, because the restra
ints upon the external person of the one
 being
 regenerated are in the hands of the
 Divine Truth within, he is open to
 receive all that acc
ords with the Divine. He is open
 to take in through his understanding the per
ceptions of love and righteousness. Indeed
, because of this:
 the appearances of worldly glory — the
 external truths of those who rule,
 int
erwoven with the sem
blance of celest
ial good but
 serving
 self
-love; and the external truths
 of persuasive sensuality, int
erwoven with self-love and knowledge
 made beautiful
 for the form of concupiscence
 — at first these were attractive before the
 understanding of the one being reformed
. Yet now, by the power of
 the Divine Truth that has suffused him
 and dwells within
 his external person, he has humbled
 concupiscence, the ruling principle
 of the natural mind. The displays of
 concupiscence have become loath
some in the presence of the righteous
. However, the aspects of the Divine
, of righteousness, of humility
, and of despised and lowly
 truths are pleasing to him.


**¶26.** Again
, the faculty of obedience was
 at first opening to empty falsities and
 to the enticements of concup
iscence, to the hidden persu
asions of wickedness. All these
 were pleasing at first, at the
 time when he received them. Yet now
, by the power of the Divine Truth
 within, the enticements of conc
upiscence and the persuasions
 of spiritual
 s
orcery and evil secrets have become lo
athsome in his presence; he
 takes no pleasure in receiving them from this
 time on
ward. Rather, he loves at all
 times to listen
 to the influx of the teachings of
 righteousness, the words of worship and
 of prayer, the exaltation of
 praise and the teachings of truth, and
 the knowledge of charity.

**
¶27.** Simply:
 all the openings of the mind in
 similar fashion were at one time opening to
 wickedness, but now have opened to
 the good. Evil was ruling in the
 external person during that time, doing whatever
 it pleased, with
 no authority
 above it.

**¶28
.** Yet now, authority has been
 taken from Evil
 in the faculties of the external person
. The Living Divine Proceeding has
 become lord over all its capacities.
 It has bound them with a bond of
 heavenly peace, and sealed them with
 the confirmation of Divine Truth. It has
 opened the faculties of the external person
 to the good, and because of this
 the good enters through obedience and
 through
 understanding. It dwells in the will
. The Holy Proceeding reigns
. It accomplishes all that it purposes
. It annuls the will of Evil
, from its
 origin
 to its
 final
 effects
. In its
 place, the will of the Holy
 Proceeding comes about, and the purpose
 of the Divine Truth within.

**
¶29.** With wisdom and
 discernment make yourselves secure at
 the circuit of the mind's openings
, so that the evil dwelling in the
 external person has no power over you —
 so
 that it cannot seize your
 wisdom, nor scatter it from faculty to
 faculty, nor drive it from state to
 state in manif
old disgu
ises.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [, the sin came up in the fruits and went in to the rulers.]

The sin that s[purted out from the rulers,] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [fruits of the tree]. It went in to the rulers [and assumed them, and] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[ted the limbs of the body, and they] begat each of them according to his destiny [and his likeness to the image]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.
Behold, I have taught you this lesson, how the rulers shaped Adam and Eve by the action of the sin that went into the[m] through the fruits, and he was ordained after the image of the exalted one.

The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.
In this way his faculty [has its] outer [limbs] to look at [and to receive in] every type with[in its storehouses.]

Also [the fa]culty of the eyes [has] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the] time and think and seek [after the image that it received,] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t]ed it—whether it be something from lu[st and evil desire, or a]n image of love [or of fair appearance, or something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.

The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [inner chambers] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.

[In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [to its cavities] and [search its] storehouse and remember [and bring forth] only these things.

However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [it be good or evil,] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.

Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.

And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.

For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.

Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [they will ask it for their deposit, it shall bring it out and give it to them.]
[For it shall find each thing] in the place that it put it.

This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.

Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.

Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds is also of this same type;] they shall bring it out in to [the one who seeks it.] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!

Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [and doors] that [must be passed, and] there are a mass [of bolts upon] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [that seal them] are [very many.] Whenever someone will wish [to bring out what is within, the guard who holds] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.

This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.

However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.

Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.

So, now, bec[ause] the b[olt]s to the body of the righteous person are in the hands of the Light M[in]d within, he is open [to receive] in all that is pleasing to God. He is op[en to take] in by his eyes the visions of lov[e and truth] and righteousness. Indeed, due to this, the si[ghts and] the [ad]ornme[nt of the gar]ments of kings, which are woven with gold; and the garments of silken wom[en], which are woven with gold and pearls, made beautiful for the shape of lust; first they were lovable before the eyes of the chosen person. Yet, now, by the power of the Light Mind that has suffused him and lived in the body he has humbled lust, the goddess of the body. The parades of lust have become loathsome in the presence of the righteous person. How-ever, the aspects of divinity and righteousness and humility and scorned clothes are pleasing to him.

Again, [these] ears were first opening to empty sounds and to the melodies of lust, to the secrecies of [wic]kedness. All these were pleasing at first, at the time when he he[a]rd them. Yet, now, by the power of the Light Mind, the sounds of lust and the words of magic and evil mysteries have become loathsome in his presence; as he is not pleased to hear them from this time on. Rather, he likes all the time to listen to the sounds of the lessons of righteousness, the words of the psalms and of the prayers, the praise of the hymns and the lessons of truth, and the knowledge of charity.

[S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.

With wisdom and skill make yourselves secure at the circuit of the body's orifices, so that the sin that dwells in the body has no power over you. Nor does it take from you your light, nor scatter it from place to place, nor (drive) it from site to site in various forms.

[... in the] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [ ... ].

Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [S]in, the begin-ning and the end. [In contrast], the will of the [Holly Spir[it] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.
